messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-warp tiler prototype for FlashMix v2 on A100s. Short summary: reduced shared-mem spills, lower DRAM bandwidth for larger microbatches, but saw a regression on tiny-batch long-seq (batch=1, seq=4096). Uploading perf traces and a short benchmark table. (thread_ts 1801234567)

anand: Can you share the nsys slice and the exact batch/seq shapes you tested? Also curious about KV cache config.

maria: Pasted test shapes: microbatch_sizes = [1,4,8], seq_lens = [512,2048,4096]. KV cache enabled with LRU-ish eviction, prefetch_count=2 by default. Kernel routing: flashmix_v2 used for most batch8 cases, fallback to fused_attention for batch1 in a few shapes.

jess: Did you change pipeline staging or occupancy targets when enabling the tiler?

maria: Yes — switched to a 3-stage pipeline (load/compute/store). Tiler params: tile_width=128, tile_height=32, warps_per_tile=4. Target occupancy ~0.75. That reduced smem thrash in the mid-range but increased bank-contention at the extremes.

benchbot: Quick benchmark summary (ns/step, tokens/s, DRAM GB/s):
```
# flashbaseline v1.6 (A100)
batch=8 seq=2048 -> 42ms, 95k tokens/s, DRAM=320 GB/s
batch=1 seq=4096 -> 280ms, 14k tokens/s, DRAM=410 GB/s

# flashmix_v2 + crosswarp-tiler (A100)
batch=8 seq=2048 -> 39ms, 103k tokens/s, DRAM=260 GB/s  # ~+8% perf, -19% bandwidth
batch=1 seq=4096 -> 308ms, 12.7k tokens/s, DRAM=430 GB/s   # regression on tiny batch
```

anand: Interesting. KV cache behaviour? Did prefetch_count cause extra writes/evictions under many concurrent contexts? I ask because evictions can spike DRAM.

maria: Observed eviction thrash at ~4k concurrent contexts when prefetch_count=2. Memory traffic trace shows many small writes during store stage. Switched heuristic: if median_seq < 512 then prefetch_count=0 else prefetch_count=2. Quick win — memory traffic down ~18% in mixed workloads.

tom: Any visibility into smem bank conflicts or per-SM stall reasons for the batch1 regression?

maria: Yes — nsys flame and bank-conflict heatmap shows high bank_util spikes when tile_width=256 for long seqs at tiny batch. Seems the tiler mapping spreads accesses across warps in a way that creates non-coalesced patterns for KV store.

jess: Could we auto-tune tile_width based on recent request distribution? Maybe sample seq percentiles and pick a mapping.

maria: I prototyped a lightweight estimator that samples recent sequences and picks tile_width accordingly. Pseudo below:
```python
seqs = sample_recent_requests(200)  # last 200 requests
p75 = np.percentile(seqs, 75)
if p75 > 1024:
    tile_width = 256
elif p75 > 512:
    tile_width = 128
else:
    tile_width = 64
# rollout as a canary feature flag
```

benchbot: Trace uploaded: /runs/1801234567/nsys_trace_report.json and heatmap at /runs/1801234567/smem_heatmap.png

anand: Next action items I propose:
- run full regression suite on T4 and A100 against baseline flash v1.6 (matrix of batch x seq)
- run KV eviction vs prefetch sweep to build curve (prefetch_count 0..4)
- measure tail latency for canary pool with estimator on/off

jess: Also add smem bank-conflict heatmap to infra dashboard and a histogram of per-kernel DRAM bytes. That'll help ops correlate.

maria: Will push artifacts + PR. Plan: feature-flag crosswarp_tiler (off by default for hosted), add estimator behind opt-in, and add perf tests to CI. I'll also add a guard: if tiny_batch & long_seq then prefer fused_attention path.

tom: SGTM. Thanks for the deep dive — please tag me on the PR. :thumbsup:

maria: Will do. Uploading PR shortly with traces + unit perf tests.
